headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Langflow’s server-side flow execution can expose secrets and feed unverified outputs into the course agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and chain tools in graph-based flows, while the course agent also reads/writes files and exposes stdin/stdout plus API endpoints. A shared workspace or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or uploaded file set, prompt-like content can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions, injected text can steer downstream tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and upload directories for each agent.
Disable automatic instruction-following on file contents.
Add a manual review step before any tool execution triggered by file text.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs where possible.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow explicitly handles per-flow component credentials and broad network egress, and the course agent handles research data plus configuration secrets. If they share files or server-side state, sensitive inputs can be exposed through Langflow’s flows or the course agent’s outputs. Because both profiles show secret handling and filesystem access, the leakage pathway is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, Langflow can ingest files containing secrets or research data.
IF Langflow flows call external model providers or HTTP services with those files, contents can leave the local boundary.
IF the course agent writes secrets into shared outputs, Langflow can read them back.
mitigations: Store secrets in separate vaults, not in shared files.
Remove shared write access between the two runtimes.
Redact secrets before any file handoff.
Restrict Langflow flows to non-sensitive inputs only.
Audit outbound requests from both agents for secret-bearing payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and install packages. Langflow also runs server-side Python code unsandboxed by default, while the course agent uses local Docker Compose. That overlap creates a realistic write-conflict and environment-drift risk even without git writes, especially if they target the same directory or container volume.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mounted volume, file clobbering can occur.
IF both install packages into the same environment, dependency drift can break one or both runs.
IF Langflow Python components run unsandboxed in the same host context, they can interfere with the course agent’s local setup.
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments or containers.
Mount distinct output directories per agent.
Pin dependencies and avoid shared package installs.
Run Langflow code components in a sandboxed container.
Add file-locking or single-writer discipline for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a multi-agent orchestration system that can chain outputs through flow nodes, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints that can consume generated text. If Langflow-produced facts or instructions are fed into the course agent without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or content. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so I keep the severity high but not critical.
conditions: IF Langflow output is passed into the course agent’s ask or agentic-ask endpoints, unverified claims can propagate.
IF the course agent uses Langflow-generated text as authoritative context, downstream answers or actions can be wrong at scale.
IF either agent auto-executes tool calls from the other’s output, errors can trigger further actions.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require citations or source IDs before downstream use.
Limit automatic tool execution from generated text.
Log and review cross-agent handoffs.
Use a human approval gate for any action-taking output.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored component credentials, while the course agent touches academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. Their retention and secret-handling practices are not aligned in the profiles, so a shared deployment could create mismatched logging or residency handling. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pair’s combined data flow.
conditions: IF the same data class is logged by both agents with different retention periods, compliance mismatch occurs.
IF EU or regulated data is routed through Langflow flows that retain credentials or intermediate outputs, policy violations can occur.
IF the course agent’s secrets are stored in shared logs, deletion and export obligations become harder to satisfy.
mitigations: Align retention settings across both systems.
Disable verbose logging for secrets and intermediate outputs.
Separate regulated data from general research data.
Document data-flow ownership for each agent.
Review residency and deletion requirements before deployment.
